subject.title: fix(acpx): keep leaked non-openai model out of the Codex ACP thinking slot

question: Should OpenClaw accept this provenance-aware Codex ACP policy: drop unsupported inherited defaults, but fail closed for explicit unsupported model selections, using the new optional ACP runtime fields?
rationale: The patch appears correct, but it changes a compatibility-sensitive ACP runtime contract and provider/model routing behavior that should be owned by the ACP reviewer rather than by automation alone.

options.title: Approve the current policy after refresh
options.body: Accept the additive runtime fields and provenance-aware drop/fail behavior, then clear the stale review state and merge after current-head gates pass.

options.title: Require a compatibility variant
options.body: Ask for a narrower migration or compatibility proof if maintainers want older or external ACP backends explicitly covered before merge.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged if maintainers want to redesign the ACP model-routing contract instead of extending it here.

recommendation.title: Approve the current policy after refresh
recommendation.body: Accept the additive runtime fields and provenance-aware drop/fail behavior, then clear the stale review state and merge after current-head gates pass.
